title: Extension from an ideal-power submodule over a fixed complement
statement: Let X be a locally Noetherian quasi-compact scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], I a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, F a quasi-coherent module, and G a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent]. For n >= 0 use the image-defined product I^n G [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk], with its inclusion j_n into G. Let U be any open whose points are exactly those where the stalk inclusion I_x -> O_X,x is surjective. Every O_U-linear map psi:G|U -> F|U extends from some I^n G: there exist n >= 0 and chi:I^n G -> F with j_n|U followed by psi equal to chi|U [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Only this finite-stage surjectivity is asserted, not injectivity or a colimit comparison.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open), surjectivity paragraphs

proof.text: *Step 2 (finiteness facts on the Noetherian scheme $X$).* (a) $X$ is quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] and quasi-compact, and every open $V\subseteq X$ is quasi-compact: given an open cover $(V_j)$ of $V$, the set of closed sets $X\setminus(V_{j_1}\cup\dots\cup V_{j_k})$ has a minimal element $X\setminus V_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]; then $V_0\cup V_j=V_0$ for all $j$, so $V_0=V$. (b) $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent of finite type (generated by $1$), hence coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]; each $\mathcal I^n$ is a quasi-coherent submodule of it [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections](1), hence coherent [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](2), hence of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]; likewise $\mathcal I^n\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal G$ is coherent. (c) A coherent $\mathcal M$ is of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation](2): near each point there is a surjection $\pi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus a}\to\mathcal M|_V$ whose kernel is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], so on a smaller neighbourhood $V'$ a surjection $\mathcal O_{V'}^{\oplus b}\to\ker\pi|_{V'}$, and the composite $\alpha:\mathcal O_{V'}^{\oplus b}\to\mathcal O_{V'}^{\oplus a}$ has cokernel $\mathcal M|_{V'}$. (d) $\mathcal T_n=\mathcal I^n\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G$ is coherent: it is quasi-coherent with $\mathcal T_n(W)\cong\mathcal I^n(W)\otimes_A\mathcal G(W)$ for affine $W$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections]; both factors are finitely generated $A$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](c) by (b), so is their tensor product, so $\mathcal T_n$ is of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](c) and coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open, line 2621), the finiteness hypotheses used tacitly when the proof applies Properties 01PQ, Lemmas 01Y8, 01YA and 'By Lemma 01XZ the sheaf G is of finite presentation'

proof.text: *Step 4 (reduction of surjectivity of $\rho^0$ to coherent $\mathcal F$).* Suppose $\rho^0$ is surjective for every coherent module, and let $\mathcal F$ be quasi-coherent and $s\in\mathcal F(U)$. $\mathcal F|_U$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2); let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal F|_U$ be the image of the $\mathcal O_U$-linear map $\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal F|_U$, $1\mapsto s$. It is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image](2) and on affine $W\subseteq U$ its sections are $\mathcal O_X(W)\,s|_W$ (ibid. (3)), generated by one element, so $\mathcal S$ is of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](c). Since $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $U$ is quasi-compact (Step 2(a)), [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-submodule-extension] gives a quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal G'\subseteq\mathcal F$ of finite type with $\mathcal G'|_U=\mathcal S$; so $s\in\mathcal G'(U)$, and $\mathcal G'$ is coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. By hypothesis there are $n$ and $\chi':\mathcal I^n\to\mathcal G'$ with $\chi'_U(1)=s$; then $\chi=\iota\circ\chi':\mathcal I^n\to\mathcal F$ ($\iota$ the inclusion) has $\chi_U(1)=s$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open, line 2621), first paragraph: 'Since F is the union of its coherent submodules, see Properties, Lemma 01PG (and Lemma 01XZ) we may and do assume that F is coherent to prove surjectivity' (01PG is proved from Properties Lemma 01PF, which is used here directly)

proof.text: *Step 5 (coherent $\mathcal F$: the subsheaves $\mathcal F_N$ stabilize).* Let $\mathcal F$ be coherent. For $N\ge0$ let $\mathcal F_N\subseteq\mathcal F$ be the subsheaf of sections annihilated by $\mathcal I^N$ [lem-weil-pbc-sections-annihilated-by-ideal] (applied to the finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I^N$, Step 2(b); $\mathcal F_0=0$). It is quasi-coherent (ibid. (1)), and $\mathcal F_N\subseteq\mathcal F_{N+1}$ directly from the definition since $\mathcal I^{N+1}\subseteq\mathcal I^N$ (Step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-acc-quasi-coherent] there is $n$ with $\mathcal F_N=\mathcal F_n$ for all $N\ge n$; put $\mathcal H=\mathcal F_n$. Then $\mathcal I^n\mathcal H=0$: for affine $W$, $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal H)(W)=\mathcal I^n(W)\mathcal H(W)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections](2), and $\mathcal I^n(W)\mathcal H(W)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-sections-annihilated-by-ideal](2); a sheaf whose sections over all affine opens vanish is $0$, the affine opens being a basis [def-pc-scheme].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open, line 2621), first paragraph: 'Let F_n denote the quasi-coherent subsheaf of F consisting of sections annihilated by I^n ... F_n = F_{n+1} = ... for some n by Lemma 01Y8. Set H = F_n'

proof.text: *Step 6 (Artin-Rees: a submodule $\mathcal F'$ without $\mathcal I$-torsion and with $\mathcal F'|_U=\mathcal F|_U$).* By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-artin-rees] for $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal F$ there is $c\ge0$ with $\mathcal I^m\mathcal F\cap\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal I^{m-c}\mathcal H$ for $m\ge c$; for $m=n+c$ this gives $\mathcal I^m\mathcal F\cap\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal H=0$ (Step 5). Put $\mathcal F'=\mathcal I^m\mathcal F$, quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections](1); as in Step 1 (with $\mathcal F$ for $\mathcal G$), $\mathcal F'|_U=\mathcal F|_U$. For every $N\ge0$ the subsheaf $\mathcal F'_N$ of sections of $\mathcal F'$ annihilated by $\mathcal I^N$ is $\mathcal F'\cap\mathcal F_N$ (same defining condition), and $\mathcal F_N\subseteq\mathcal F_n=\mathcal H$ (Step 5: increasing, and constant from $n$ on); hence $\mathcal F'_N\subseteq\mathcal F'\cap\mathcal H=0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open, line 2621), first paragraph: 'By Artin-Rees (Lemma 01YA) ... Thus if we set F' = I^mF then we see that F' cap F_n = 0 and F'|_U = F|_U. Note in particular that the subsheaf (F')_N of sections annihilated by I^N is zero for all N >= 0'

proof.text: *Step 7 (surjectivity of $\rho^0$; the 'in particular' isomorphism).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sections-over-quasi-compact-open](2) to $\mathcal F'$ ($X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $\mathcal I$ of finite type: Step 2): $\varinjlim_N\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal I^N,\mathcal F'/\mathcal F'_N)\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal F')$ is bijective. Since $\mathcal F'_N=0$ (Step 6), the quotient map $\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F'/\mathcal F'_N$ is an isomorphism and the transition maps are restriction along $\mathcal I^{N+1}\subseteq\mathcal I^N$, so $\varinjlim_N\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal I^N,\mathcal F')\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal F')$, $\chi'\mapsto\chi'_U(1)$, is bijective. The square formed with $\rho^0$ for $\mathcal F$ and the maps induced by the inclusion $\iota:\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F$ commutes ($(\iota\circ\chi')_U(1)=\iota_U(\chi'_U(1))$), and $\iota_U:\mathcal F'(U)\to\mathcal F(U)$ is bijective since $\mathcal F'|_U=\mathcal F|_U$. Hence $\rho^0$ is surjective for coherent $\mathcal F$, so for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ (Step 4), and bijective (Step 3): $\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal I^n,\mathcal F)\cong\Gamma(U,\mathcal F)$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$; with Step 3 this is the parenthetical case $\mathcal G=\mathcal O_X$ of the statement.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open, line 2621), first paragraph: 'Hence by Properties, Lemma 01PQ we deduce that the top horizontal arrow in the following commutative diagram is a bijection ... we conclude that the bottom horizontal arrow is surjective as desired'

proof.text: *Step 8 (the sheaf $\mathcal E=\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$).* $\mathcal G$ is of finite presentation (Step 2(c)), so $\mathcal E=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-hom-finite-presentation-quasi-coherent], with $\mathcal E(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal G|_U,\mathcal F|_U)$ by definition, and its restriction maps are restriction of morphisms. By Steps 3-7 applied to $\mathcal E$, $\rho^0_{\mathcal E}:\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal I^n,\mathcal E)\to\mathcal E(U)$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi_U(1)$, is bijective.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open, line 2621), second paragraph: 'By Lemma 01XZ the sheaf G is of finite presentation and hence the sheaf H = SheafHom(G, F) is quasi-coherent, see Schemes, Section 01LA. By definition we have H(U) = Hom(G|_U, F|_U)'

proof.text: *Step 9 (from $\psi$ to a map on $\mathcal I^n\otimes\mathcal G$).* Let $\psi\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal G|_U,\mathcal F|_U)=\mathcal E(U)$. By Step 8 there are $n\ge0$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\varphi:\mathcal I^n\to\mathcal E$ with $\varphi_U(1)=\psi$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-hom-adjunction] $\varphi$ corresponds to $\tilde\varphi:\mathcal T=\mathcal I^n\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ with $\tilde\varphi_W(t_W(a\otimes g))=(\varphi_W(a))_W(g)$. Let $\pi:\mathcal T\to\mathcal G$ be the multiplication map, whose image is $\mathcal I^n\mathcal G$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module](0), and $\mathcal K=\ker\pi$ (sectionwise), quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. $\mathcal T$ is coherent (Step 2(d)).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open, line 2621), second paragraph: 'there exists an n >= 0 and an phi: I^n -> H which recovers psi on restriction to U. By Modules, Lemma 01CN phi corresponds to a map I^n tensor G -> F ... Consider the short exact sequence 0 -> K -> I^n tensor G -> I^nG -> 0'

proof.text: *Step 10 ($\mathcal I^n\mathcal K=0$; 'proof omitted' in the source).* Let $W$ be affine, $A=\mathcal O_X(W)$, $J=\mathcal I^n(W)$, $M=\mathcal G(W)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections] $t_W:J\otimes_AM\to\mathcal T(W)$ is bijective, and $\pi_W(t_W(j\otimes g))=jg$, so $\mathcal K(W)=t_W(\{\sum_ij_i\otimes g_i:\sum_ij_ig_i=0\})$. For $a\in J$ and such an element, $a\cdot\sum_ij_i\otimes g_i=\sum_i(j_ia)\otimes g_i=\sum_ia\otimes(j_ig_i)=a\otimes\sum_ij_ig_i=0$, moving the scalar $j_i\in A$ across $\otimes_A$ (here $j_ia=aj_i$ is read as $j_i$ times the element $a$ of $J$). So $J\,\mathcal K(W)=0$, i.e. $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal K)(W)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections](2); as affine opens form a basis [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal I^n\mathcal K=0$. On an affine write J=I^n and z=sum_i b_i tensor m_i in the kernel, so sum_i b_i m_i=0. For a in J, balancing gives a z=sum_i a tensor b_i m_i=a tensor 0=0. Thus J kills the kernel; this also applies when n=0.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open, line 2621), second paragraph: 'Note that I^nK = 0 (proof omitted)'

proof.text: *Step 11 ($\mathcal I^m\mathcal T\cong\mathcal I^{n+m}\mathcal G$).* By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-artin-rees] for $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal T$ there is $c'$ with $\mathcal I^m\mathcal T\cap\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal I^{m-c'}\mathcal K$ for $m\ge c'$; take $m=n+c'$, so $\mathcal I^m\mathcal T\cap\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal K=0$ (Step 10). Let $\pi'$ be the restriction of $\pi$ to $\mathcal I^m\mathcal T$; its kernel is $\mathcal I^m\mathcal T\cap\mathcal K=0$. Its image is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image](2) with sections over affine $W$ equal to $\pi_W((\mathcal I^m\mathcal T)(W))=\pi_W(\mathcal I(W)^m\mathcal T(W))=\mathcal I(W)^m\pi_W(\mathcal T(W))=\mathcal I(W)^m\mathcal I(W)^nM=(\mathcal I^{n+m}\mathcal G)(W)$ (ibid. (3), [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections](2), $\pi_W(\mathcal T(W))=(\mathcal I^n\mathcal G)(W)$ by (3) again). Two subsheaves of $\mathcal G$ with the same sections over all affine opens coincide (glue along an affine cover [def-pc-scheme]), so the image is $\mathcal I^{n+m}\mathcal G$, and $\pi':\mathcal I^m\mathcal T\to\mathcal I^{n+m}\mathcal G$ is a monomorphism and an epimorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, hence an isomorphism in the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open, line 2621), second paragraph: 'By Artin-Rees again we see that K cap I^m(I^n tensor G) = 0 for some m large enough. In other words we see that I^m(I^n tensor G) -> I^{n+m}G is an isomorphism'

proof.text: *Step 12 (surjectivity (S)).* Put $\varphi'=\tilde\varphi\circ j\circ\pi'^{-1}:\mathcal I^{n+m}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$, $j:\mathcal I^m\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal T$. Let $W\subseteq U$ be open and $g\in\mathcal G(W)=(\mathcal I^{n+m}\mathcal G)(W)$ (Step 1). As $1\in\mathcal I^n(W)$ (Step 1), $u=t_W(1\otimes g)\in\mathcal T(W)$, and $u\in(\mathcal I^m\mathcal T)(W)$ because $(\mathcal I^m\mathcal T)|_U=\mathcal T|_U$ (Step 1 with the quasi-coherent $\mathcal T$, Step 2(d), for $\mathcal G$). Since $\pi_W(u)=1\cdot g=g$, $\pi'^{-1}_W(g)=u$ and $\varphi'_W(g)=\tilde\varphi_W(t_W(1\otimes g))=(\varphi_W(1))_W(g)$. Since $\varphi$ is a morphism of sheaves, $\varphi_W(1)=\varphi_U(1)|_W=\psi|_W$, so $\varphi'_W(g)=\psi_W(g)$. Thus $\rho_{n+m}(\varphi')=\psi$, proving (S).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open, line 2621), second paragraph: 'Let phi' be the restriction of phi to this submodule thought of as a map I^{m+n}G -> F. Then phi' gives an element of the left hand side of the first arrow of the lemma which maps to psi via the arrow'

lean.statement:
theorem coherent_hom_ideal_power_extension {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [CompactSpace X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F G : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hG : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace G) (U : X.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ x : X, x ∈ U ↔ Function.Surjective
      ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).map I.toModulesι).hom) :
    ∀ ψ : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor X.ringCatSheaf U).obj G ⟶
        (SheafOfModules.overFunctor X.ringCatSheaf U).obj F,
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (χ : idealModuleProduct (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2 G ⟶ F),
        (SheafOfModules.overFunctor X.ringCatSheaf U).map
            (idealModuleProductι (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2 G) ≫ ψ =
          (SheafOfModules.overFunctor X.ringCatSheaf U).map χ
